items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to the disposition of abandoned animals; and to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing certified euthanasia technicians to perform certain veterinary medicine practices without a license
items.lawCode: Amd §332, Ag & Mkts L; amd §6705, Ed L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S7955

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to the disposition
of abandoned
animals;
and to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing certified
euthanasia technicians to perform certain veterinary medicine practices
without a license

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
To amend Chapter 479 of the laws of
2009 in order to make certain clarifications with regard to where an
abandoned animal may be delivered; and that certified euthanasia
technicians who are registered or euthanasia technicians in training
may practice veterinary medicine within the scope of their
certification or training without a license to practice veterinary
medicine

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Section one amends section 332 of the
agriculture and markets law, as amended by chapter 479 of the laws of
2009, by clarifying that a duly incorporated society for the
prevention of cruelty to animals shall be a duly incorporated humane
society.

Section two amends section 6705 of the education law by adding a new
subdivision 13 which adds any person certified and currently
registered as a certified euthanasia technician, or any person
undergoing training for such certification, to the list of exempt
persons who shall be permitted to practice veterinary medicine within
the state without a license, provided that such practice is limited
to that person's certification or training.

Section three provides the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:
This legislation will clarify the
specific type of
society for the prevention of cruelty to animals to which the bill
refers.

Certified and currently registered euthanasia technicians, and
technicians undergoing training for certification in the field, have
been practicing euthanasia of animals throughout the state. This
legislation codifies such practice and clarifies that such persons
are permitted by law to practice certain aspects of veterinary
medicine without a license in veterinary medicine, so long as the
practice of veterinary medicine is limited to such person's training
and certification. This legislation will further ensure that those

who practice euthanasia 01 animals - an Important practice when
practiced humanely are practitioners who are certified and
registered, or are in training to be certified, and thus are well
trained.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATION:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
On the same date and in the same manner as section
5 of chapter 479 of the laws of 2009 takes effect.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S7955A

TITLE OF BILL:
An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to the
disposition of abandoned animals; and to amend the education law, in
relation to authorizing certified euthanasia technicians to perform
certain veterinary medicine practices without a license

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
To amend Chapter 479 of the laws of 2009 in order to make certain clar-
ifications with regard to where an abandoned animal may be delivered;
and that certified euthanasia technicians who are registered or euthana-
sia technicians in training may practice veterinary medicine within the
scope of their certification or training without a license to practice
veterinary medicine

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Section one amends section 332 of the agriculture and markets law, as
amended by chapter 479 of the laws of 2009, by adding "duly incorporated
humane society" to the list of places to which a person may deliver an
abandoned animal.

Section two amends subdivisions 1 and 2 of section 374 of the agricul-
ture and markets law, as amended by chapter 479 of the laws of 2009, by
adding "duly incorporated humane society" to the list of places that may
lawfully cause to be humanely destroyed, or release for adoption,
certain abandoned animals.

Section three amends section 6705 of the education law by adding a new
subdivision 13 which adds any person certified and currently registered
as a certified euthanasia technician, or any person undergoing training
for such certification, to the list of exempt persons who shall be
permitted to practice veterinary medicine within the state without a
license, provided that such practice is limited to that person's certif-
ication or training.

Section three provides the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:
Currently duly incorporated humane societies receive, release for
adoption, or lawfully and humanely destroy certain abandoned animals in
their care.  This bill merely adds "duly incorporated humane society" to
the list of places that may carry out such practices.

Certified and currently registered euthanasia technicians, and techni-
cians undergoing training for certification in the field, have been
practicing euthanasia of animals throughout the state. This legislation
codifies such practice and clarifies that such persons are permitted by
law to practice certain aspects of veterinary medicine without a license
in veterinary medicine, so long as the practice of veterinary medicine
is limited to such person's training and certification. This legislation

will further ensure that those who practice euthanasia of animals - an
important practice when practiced humanely are practitioners who are
certified and registered, or are in training to be certified, and thus
are well trained.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATION:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
On the same date and in the same manner as section 5 of chapter 479 of
the laws of 2009 takes effect.
